blocks.text: A brokerage launch has a lot of moving parts. Here's the order we work in, and why.
01 Discovery
We start with your business model. Target markets, account types, expected volumes, the providers you already have. It saves a lot of rework later.
02 Architecture
Next we map the stack: which platform, where it's hosted, how liquidity connects and which systems need to sync with what.
03 Integration
Platform, bridge, CRM, KYC and payment providers get connected and configured. This is usually the longest stage, and the one most worth getting right.
04 Testing
Pricing, order flow, rejects, deposits, onboarding. We test the real workflows end to end before a single live client touches them.
05 Go-Live
Launch happens with monitoring already running and a clear plan for the first few days.
06 Managed Support
After launch, we stay on. Updates, configuration changes, incident response and the small adjustments every new brokerage needs in its first months.
Your trading environment is only as dependable as its weakest piece. Splitting it across unrelated vendors tends to make that weak piece hard to find. We handle the core layers together.
MT5 Platform Configuration
Server setup, trading groups, symbol specifications, margin settings and manager access, configured for your account structure from day one.
Server Hosting

Hosting with regional options, hardened access controls, scheduled backups and active monitoring. We'll talk you through latency honestly, including what hosting location can and can't do for execution.
MT4/MT5 Maintenance
Version upgrades, configuration changes, backup and restore checks, performance reviews and migrations. The routine work that keeps a platform healthy and is easy to neglect when things are busy.
Liquidity Connectivity
We connect your platform to liquidity providers through the method that suits the setup, whether that's a bridge, an MT5 gateway or a direct FIX connection.
CRM & KYC Integration
Client onboarding, identity verification and account creation linked into one workflow, so a new client moves from registration to a funded trading account without manual copying in between.

Existing Brokers

Prop Firms
Evaluation accounts, rule enforcement, risk dashboards and payout reviews need dependable infrastructure behind them. We build and support that layer.

Moving from MT4 to MT5, changing hosting, adding a second liquidity provider or replacing a CRM. Migrations like these need careful planning, and we handle them with change control and rollback options in place.
What does a forex brokerage technology provider actually do?

We supply and connect the technical systems a brokerage runs on. That includes the trading platform, servers, liquidity connectivity, CRM, KYC and payment integrations, along with ongoing support. We don't act as a broker, and we don't give investment or regulatory advice.
Can you help us launch a brokerage from scratch?

Yes. Our brokerage setup service covers platform selection, hosting, liquidity connectivity, CRM and KYC integration, testing and go-live. Licensing and regulatory approval remain your responsibility, and requirements vary by jurisdiction.
Do you only work with MT5?
MT5 is our main focus for new deployments, but we also maintain MT4 environments and help brokers plan migrations from MT4 to MT5.
What's the difference between a bridge, a gateway and a FIX connection?

All three connect your trading platform to liquidity. They differ in how orders are routed, how much control you have and how they're maintained. Which one suits you depends on your providers and execution model, and we'll walk you through the options during discovery.
Can you take over support of an existing MT5 setup?
Yes. We start with a technical review of your current configuration, hosting and integrations, then agree on a maintenance plan covering monitoring, upgrades and incident response.
Do you handle KYC and AML compliance for us?
We handle the technical integration: connecting verification providers, building the approval workflow and syncing results to your CRM. Your compliance obligations stay with your regulated business.
Can we choose only the services we need?
Absolutely. Our forex brokerage technology is modular. Some clients come to us only for hosting or liquidity connectivity, while others want the full stack.
Tell us where your brokerage is today and where you want it to be. We'll look at your current setup, point out the gaps and suggest a practical path forward. No obligation, and no hard sell.

sections.title: What Goes Into a Technology-Led Launch

blocks.text: Every project gets scoped around your model, so no two look identical. That said, most launches cover the same core layers.
Choosing and Configuring the Platform

First question: full MT5 deployment or white label? A white label usually costs less and gets you live sooner. A full deployment gives you more control. We'll help you weigh it up against your budget and where you want to be in two or three years.
Once that's decided, we configure the platform properly. Trading groups, account types, symbol specs, leverage and margin rules, and manager access for your dealing and support teams.
Servers and Infrastructure

Your platform needs somewhere to live. We set up hosting in a region that makes sense for your clients and your liquidity, lock down access, schedule backups and get monitoring running before launch day. A backup server and a recovery plan are built in from the start, because adding them later is always harder.
Connecting Liquidity

Depending on what your providers support and how you plan to execute, we'll connect through a bridge, an MT5 gateway or a direct FIX connection. Symbols get mapped. Price feeds get checked. Orders route the way your risk policy says they should.
CRM, KYC and Payments

This is the bit your clients actually notice. Registration, identity checks, account creation, deposits and withdrawals all have to work together, and they all have to talk to the trading platform. We connect your CRM, KYC provider and payment providers so a new client goes from sign-up to a funded account in one smooth flow.
Testing Before Anyone Goes Live

We test everything against real scenarios. Price feeds, order execution, rejects, margin calls, onboarding, deposits, withdrawals, reporting. Finding a problem at this stage costs very little. Finding it after your first hundred clients arrive is a different story.
Support After Launch
The first few weeks are when small issues tend to pop up. We keep a close eye on things during that period, tweak settings as real trading comes in, and then move you onto an ongoing support plan.
There's a reason we do things in this order. Each stage relies on the one before it, and jumping ahead nearly always means redoing work.
01 Scoping
We get to know the business. Your target markets, account types, expected client numbers, execution model and any providers you've already picked. By the end, we both know exactly what's being built.
02 Stack Design

Then we draw up the technical blueprint. Platform, hosting region, liquidity method, CRM, KYC and payment providers, and how they all connect. You see the full plan and timeline before any build work begins.
03 Build and Configuration
Servers get provisioned, the platform gets configured, liquidity gets connected. Your trading environment starts to take real shape here.
04 Integration

CRM, KYC and payment systems are linked to the platform and to each other. We also chase your third-party providers for credentials, sandbox access and technical details. Honestly, this is where most launches get delayed when nobody owns it.
05 User Acceptance Testing
Your team and ours run through every client and back-office workflow in a test environment. Anything that breaks gets fixed and retested. We sign off together.
06 Go-Live and Early Support
Launch day happens with monitoring switched on and our engineers close by. After the first stretch, we agree on an ongoing support plan that fits how you operate.
Here's the stack in a single line:
Client → Website & Client Portal → CRM, KYC & Payments → MT5 Trading Server → Bridge / Gateway / FIX → Liquidity Providers → Reporting & Back Office

A client signs up on your website. The CRM records them, the KYC provider verifies them, the payment provider handles their deposit. Their trading account opens on MT5. When they trade, orders travel through your connectivity layer to liquidity, and the results flow back into your reports.
If one link is set up badly, everything downstream feels it. So we build and test the whole chain as one system.
* MT5 server deployment, white label configuration and manager setup
* Hosting across regions, with security hardening, monitoring and backups
* Bridge, gateway and FIX connectivity, including symbol mapping and price-feed checks
* Primary and backup liquidity routes where needed
* CRM integration for leads, client records, trading accounts and IB tracking
* KYC integration with approval and rejection workflows plus audit trails
* Payment provider integration for deposits and withdrawals, including webhooks and reconciliation
* Structured testing with documented test cases and sign-off
* Monitoring after launch and a handover to managed support
Starting From Nothing

A founder has a solid business plan and a licence application underway, but no technology at all. We scope the stack, time the build alongside the regulatory process and have everything tested and waiting for when approval lands.
Turning a Partner Network Into a Brokerage

An introducing broker with a strong client base wants its own brand. We set up an MT5 white label, connect liquidity and build onboarding that makes moving existing clients over as painless as possible.
Opening a Second Entity

An established group wants a separate brokerage for a new market. We design infrastructure that reuses what already works, while keeping the new entity's servers, data and client flows properly apart.
Launches go smoother when everyone knows who owns which piece. Usually it splits like this.
What We Take Care Of
Technology planning, platform configuration, hosting setup, liquidity connectivity, CRM, KYC and payment integrations, testing, go-live support and ongoing maintenance where agreed.
What Stays With You
Company formation, licensing and regulatory approval, compliance policies, commercial agreements with liquidity and payment providers, banking, marketing and client support.
Third-Party Providers

Platform vendors, liquidity providers, KYC services and payment providers all run their own systems on their own terms. We handle the technical integration. Their service levels and contracts remain between you and them.

One more thing worth saying clearly: regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction. We can explain how technology choices relate to common regulatory expectations, but legal and compliance advice should come from qualified specialists in your target market.
How long does a forex brokerage setup take?

That depends on scope, and on how fast third-party providers respond. A white label with standard integrations moves quicker than a full MT5 deployment with several payment providers and multiple liquidity connections. After scoping, we'll give you a timeline based on what you actually need.
Do I need a licence before the technology work starts?

Not always. Plenty of clients start building while their licence application is still in progress, so everything's ready once approval comes through. Whether you need a licence, and which one, depends on your jurisdiction and business model. A regulatory advisor is the right person for that question.
Full MT5 setup or white label. Which one should I pick?

White label is generally cheaper upfront and faster to launch. A full deployment gives you more control over configuration and infrastructure. We'll go through the trade-offs with you during scoping, based on your budget and growth plans.
Can you work with providers I've already chosen?
Yes. If you've already signed with a liquidity provider, KYC service or payment provider, we build around them. Haven't chosen yet? We can walk you through the technical points worth comparing.
What happens if something goes wrong after launch?

During the early support period, our team watches your environment closely and responds to issues directly. After that, you move onto ongoing maintenance covering monitoring, configuration changes and incident response.
Can I start small and add more later?
Yes, and it's often the smarter way to go. We build the stack so extra liquidity providers, payment methods, a mobile app or new regions can be added later without rebuilding what's already there.
What does it cost to start a forex brokerage?

Technology costs depend on your platform choice, hosting, the number of integrations and the level of support you want. Licensing, legal, banking and marketing come on top of that and vary a lot by jurisdiction. fullBlocks.text: How the Setup Process Works

01 Scoping
We get to know the business. Your target markets, account types, expected client numbers, execution model and any providers you've already picked. By the end, we both know exactly what's being built.
02 Stack Design

Then we draw up the technical blueprint. Platform, hosting region, liquidity method, CRM, KYC and payment providers, and how they all connect. You see the full plan and timeline before any build work begins.
03 Build and Configuration
Servers get provisioned, the platform gets configured, liquidity gets connected. Your trading environment starts to take real shape here.
04 Integration

CRM, KYC and payment systems are linked to the platform and to each other. We also chase your third-party providers for credentials, sandbox access and technical details. Honestly, this is where most launches get delayed when nobody owns it.
05 User Acceptance Testing
Your team and ours run through every client and back-office workflow in a test environment. Anything that breaks gets fixed and retested. We sign off together.

Launch day happens with monitoring switched on and our engineers close by. After the first stretch, we agree on an ongoing support plan that fits how you operate.

Client → Website & Client Portal → CRM, KYC & Payments → MT5 Trading Server → Bridge / Gateway / FIX → Liquidity Providers → Reporting & Back Office

sections.title: What an MT5 White Label Actually Means

blocks.text: There's a fair bit of confusion around this term, so let's keep it simple.

MT5 runs on a server operated under a licence from the platform developer. With a full licence, you own and run that server yourself. That gives you the most control, but it also comes with a large upfront cost and a lot of technical responsibility.

With a white label, your brokerage operates within an existing licensed MT5 environment. You get your own branded setup, your own client groups and manager access to run your business day to day. The core server sits under the licence holder's arrangement rather than yours.

Your trading server is the one piece of your brokerage that simply can't have a bad day. When it slows down, clients notice. When it goes offline, they start calling, and some of them start looking elsewhere.

Our forex broker hosting gives your MT4 or MT5 platform infrastructure that's sized for real trading activity, secured properly and watched closely, with backups and a recovery plan that actually get tested.

sections.title: Why Reliable Hosting Matters for a Brokerage

blocks.text: Think about a major news release. Thousands of clients log in at once, prices move fast and orders pour in within seconds. That's exactly when weak hosting shows itself. Terminals freeze, history won't load, orders hang.

A regular website can get away with a slow afternoon. A trading server can't. It has to handle sudden spikes, stay connected to liquidity without interruption and keep client data safe the whole time.

General web hosts rarely understand this. They'll sell you a server, but they won't know how MT5 components fit together, why server location matters for liquidity, or what to do when your platform stops responding at 2am during the Asian session.
* Brokers preparing to launch and setting up their first trading environment
* Brokers on general-purpose hosting who keep hitting slowdowns during busy markets
* Businesses running MT4 and MT5 side by side and wanting both managed in one place
* Brokers with no real disaster recovery plan, or one nobody has ever tested
* Prop firms whose account numbers are growing faster than their current servers can handle

MT4 is still widely used, and plenty of brokers keep it running alongside MT5 for clients who prefer it. Its setup is simpler, usually a main server supported by data centre access points that clients connect through.

That simplicity doesn't mean it can be neglected. We host MT4 environments with sensible resource allocation, access points placed close to your clients, regular backups and monitoring. If you're planning an eventual move to MT5, we'll set things up so both platforms can run together during the transition.
MT5 is built differently. It splits work across several types of servers, typically a main trade server, history servers, access servers for client connections and backup servers ready to step in.

That spread gives MT5 more flexibility and resilience, but it also means more parts to place and manage well. We design your MT5 server hosting around how each component should sit, where access points should go to suit your client base, and how backup servers are kept in sync so failover works when it matters.
Server Infrastructure

Properly sized servers for your platform and expected volumes, whether that's cloud, virtual or dedicated hardware. We size for busy market conditions, not quiet Tuesday afternoons, and leave room to grow.
Location Planning

Label: Market Access Infrastructure

Every quote your clients see and every trade they place depends on one thing working quietly in the background: the line between your trading platform and the market. When that line is clean, nobody thinks about it. When it isn't, you hear about it within minutes.

We engineer that line. Our team plugs your MT4 or MT5 server into the forex liquidity sources you've chosen, configures how orders travel, and keeps a close watch on everything once real money starts flowing.
Quick clarification before going further. We don't supply liquidity ourselves. We build and look after the technical plumbing that links your platform to the providers you contract with.

blocks.text: Put simply, liquidity is the availability of buyers and sellers ready to trade at a given price. For a brokerage, it usually arrives through a liquidity provider. That might be a bank, a prime broker, a prime-of-prime firm or a non-bank market maker, each streaming bid and ask prices and accepting orders against them.

Your clients never deal with those institutions directly. They trade on your platform. Your platform, in turn, needs a reliable technical route to the provider so prices come in accurately and orders go out quickly. That route is what we mean by connectivity, and it's where a surprising number of brokerage problems begin.

sections.title: Who Comes to Us for This

blocks.text: * Startups wiring up their very first provider ahead of launch
* Established brokers wanting a second source for depth or as a safety net
* Firms switching providers and needing zero downtime during the changeover
* Operations troubled by unexplained rejects, odd spreads or quotes that stop updating
* Prop trading businesses needing external pricing or hedging links
* Brokers ready to graduate from a single feed to a multi-provider pool
Here's the journey of a single trade, in plain terms.

A client clicks buy on EUR/USD. Their order lands on your MT4 or MT5 server. Depending on your rules, the server either fills it internally or passes it onward through a connector, which might be a bridge, a gateway plugin or a direct FIX session. The connector translates the order into a format your provider understands and sends it across. The provider fills it and returns a confirmation. That confirmation travels back along the same path, the client's position appears on screen, and your reporting records what happened.
All of that typically takes a fraction of a second. Each hop, though, is a spot where a wrong setting can cause trouble.
Liquidity Provider Integration

Before touching any configuration, we gather your provider's technical documentation. Supported protocols, session schedules, instrument lists, minimum and maximum order sizes, permitted order types, and whatever conformance testing they insist on. We flag mismatches early, while they're still cheap to resolve.
Liquidity Bridge Setup

A bridge is middleware that sits between your server and one or more providers. It typically handles markups, routing logic, risk-based splitting of flow and multi-source pricing. We install it, configure it to your instructions and connect it at both ends. This is especially useful if you plan to grow beyond one provider.
MT5 Gateway Configuration

Where a provider offers a native MT5 gateway, it can be a lighter, more direct option with fewer moving pieces. Fine for straightforward setups with a single source and simple routing. We'll tell you honestly whether a gateway is enough or whether a bridge would serve you better.
FIX API Connectivity

FIX, short for Financial Information eXchange, is the protocol institutions use to swap price and order messages. Most bridges and many gateways speak FIX under the hood. We establish and certify these sessions, sort out network routing, credentials and heartbeats, and make sure reconnection behaves sensibly after a drop.
Liquidity Aggregation

With two or more providers, aggregation merges their price streams into a single book. Orders can then route by best price, by fixed allocation or by whatever logic you specify. It can tighten what clients see and spread your dependence. It also introduces extra settings to manage, which we'll explain upfront.
MT4 and MT5 Integration

Whichever platform you run, or both, we link it with your chosen connector, aligning account groups, execution modes and the way fills are reported back. Brokers running MT4 and MT5 in parallel can share a single bridge, so pricing stays consistent across the two.
Symbol Mapping

Providers and platforms rarely name or size instruments identically. One might list gold in ounces, another in lots of a hundred. Suffixes differ. Decimal places differ. Session hours differ. We line up every instrument manually and verify contract size, precision, trading hours and margin currency for each. Sloppy mapping is a classic source of costly mistakes, so this gets real attention.
Order Routing

You decide your execution model. Pass everything to the market, keep some flow internally, or use a hybrid split based on account group, trade size or client profile. We translate those decisions into working rules, test them and document them so your dealing team knows exactly what's configured.
Monitoring

After go-live, we track feed freshness, session status, fill rates, rejection counts and round-trip timing to each provider. Unusual patterns trigger alerts for our engineers, and you get a clear explanation of what happened if something needs investigating.

blocks.text: Fewer Client Complaints

Most "the platform is broken" tickets trace back to connectivity: frozen prices, mysterious rejects, fills that don't match the chart. A carefully built link removes the technical causes behind many of them.
Protection From Single Points of Failure
A backup provider with tested failover keeps clients trading if one source goes dark.
Freedom to Grow
A well-structured bridge makes adding providers, instruments or a second platform far less disruptive later on.
Clear Visibility
Monitoring and documentation mean your team understands exactly how orders flow, rather than relying on settings nobody remembers.
Our Responsibilities
Technical review of providers, connector setup, FIX sessions, symbol mapping, configuring routing per your instructions, testing, certification support, launch and ongoing monitoring.
Your Responsibilities

Selecting and contracting with providers, negotiating commercial terms, setting your execution model and risk policy, and meeting any regulatory duties on order handling and best execution in your jurisdiction.
Provider Responsibilities

Spreads, depth, fill quality and uptime are determined by your providers and by market conditions. We can't guarantee those outcomes. We have no affiliation with or endorsement from any provider, bridge vendor or the MT4/MT5 platform developer unless expressly stated.
Do you provide liquidity directly?
No. We're a technology firm. We connect your platform to providers you hold agreements with.
Do I need a bridge, or will an MT5 gateway do?

For one provider and uncomplicated routing, a gateway is often enough. Multiple sources, aggregation, markups or hybrid execution usually call for a bridge. We'll assess your plans and recommend accordingly.
What is FIX API in forex?

It's the messaging standard used across institutional trading to stream prices and transmit orders. Your bridge or gateway typically communicates with providers through FIX sessions that we set up and certify.
How does liquidity aggregation help a broker?
By combining prices from several providers, aggregation can offer clients tighter quotes and reduce reliance on any single source. It requires more configuration and monitoring, which we handle.
How long does it take to connect a provider?

Timelines vary with the connection method, the number of instruments and how quickly the provider schedules certification. Provider-side steps frequently take the longest. We'll estimate after reviewing their documentation.
Can you fix problems in an existing liquidity setup?
Yes. We audit current mappings, routing rules and connector settings, identify what's causing the issues and correct them, then document the cleaned-up configuration.
Can MT4 and MT5 share the same liquidity?
Yes. A single bridge can serve both platforms, keeping pricing aligned while you run them side by side.
Will you guarantee my spreads or execution?
No. Pricing and fills come from your providers and the market. Our job is to make sure the technology carrying your forex liquidity is accurate, stable and well monitored.

Label: Onboarding & Verification Technology

Verification is the first real conversation a new client has with your brokerage. If it's clumsy, slow or confusing, a good number of people simply give up and go elsewhere. If it's too loose, you're exposed to fraud, bad actors and serious regulatory trouble.

Our KYC AML integration work helps you strike that balance. We link identity checks, document review and screening services into your onboarding, connect the results to your CRM and trading platform, and give your compliance team a tidy, traceable workflow to act on.

sections.title: Why Brokers Need This Done Properly

blocks.text: Most brokerages start out verifying clients by hand. A passport photo arrives by email, someone eyeballs it, a utility bill follows a day later, and approval gets noted in a spreadsheet. That's manageable at twenty sign-ups a week. At two hundred, it falls apart.

Manual handling also leaves gaps. Documents get lost in inboxes. Nobody's sure who approved which client. Expired IDs go unnoticed. And when a regulator or banking partner asks to see your onboarding records, pulling together a coherent answer takes days.
Integrated verification fixes the mechanics. Your compliance people still make the calls that need human judgement, but the collecting, checking, routing and record-keeping run on rails.
* Brokers launching soon who want verification built in from the first client
* Firms whose compliance staff are drowning in manual document checks
* Brokerages expanding into countries with different ID types and onboarding rules
* Businesses that failed a banking or payment provider review over weak onboarding records
* Prop firms that need to verify traders before releasing funded accounts or payouts
The Verification Workflow

We design the path a client takes from registration to approval. What gets collected, in what order, what happens automatically and where a human reviewer steps in. Requirements can vary by country, account type or risk level, so a client in one jurisdiction might see a different flow from a client in another.
Identity and Document Verification

We connect your chosen verification provider so clients can photograph their ID, take a selfie for a liveness check and upload proof of address straight from their phone or browser. The provider checks document authenticity, compares faces and extracts data, then passes the outcome back to your systems.
Sanctions, PEP and Risk Screening

Where your providers support it, we link screening against sanctions lists, politically exposed person databases and adverse media sources. Matches get flagged for your team to investigate rather than silently blocking or passing a client.
Risk Scoring Inputs

Country of residence, screening results, source of funds answers, account type and other factors can feed a risk rating that decides whether a client sails through or lands in an enhanced review queue. The scoring rules come from your compliance policy. We wire them in.
Approval and Rejection Handling

Reviewers work from a single queue showing documents, check results and flags side by side. They can approve, reject with a reason, or ask the client for something more. Clients are told what's needed without having to email support.
CRM and Platform Sync

Verification status lives on the client profile in your CRM. Approval can automatically unlock deposits or trading account creation on MT4 or MT5, while a pending or rejected status keeps those doors closed. No one has to remember to flip a switch.
Audit Trail

Every upload, automated result, reviewer decision and status change is logged with time and user. When an auditor, bank or regulator asks how a particular client was onboarded, the answer takes minutes to retrieve.
Ongoing Checks

Verification doesn't end at approval. Expiring documents can trigger reminders to clients, and periodic rescreening can be scheduled where your provider supports it, so client records don't quietly go out of date.

Why Brokers Need This Done Properly

Most brokerages start out verifying clients by hand. A passport photo arrives by email, someone eyeballs it, a utility bill follows a day later, and approval gets noted in a spreadsheet. That's manageable at twenty sign-ups a week. At two hundred, it falls apart.

The provider checks document authenticity, compares faces and extracts data, then passes the outcome back to your systems.

Where your providers support it, we link screening against sanctions lists, politically exposed person databases and adverse media sources. Matches get flagged for your team to investigate rather than silently blocking or passing a client.

Label: Funding Infrastructure

Money moving in and out is where client trust gets won or lost. A deposit that takes hours to show up in a trading account makes people nervous. A withdrawal stuck in limbo makes them angry. And a finance team reconciling payments line by line against bank statements is a finance team that never gets ahead.

We connect your forex payment gateway providers to your CRM and trading platform so deposits credit quickly, withdrawals follow a controlled approval path, and every transaction can be traced from the client's click to the final balance.

sections.title: Why Payments Are Harder for Brokers

blocks.text: Online shops take a payment and ship a product. Brokers deal with something messier. Money arrives in many currencies, through many methods, from clients in many countries. It has to land in the correct trading account, often within minutes. Then, unlike most businesses, you also have to send money back out, regularly and securely, after checking it's going to the right person.

On top of that, forex is treated as higher risk by many payment companies, so brokers often end up juggling several providers. Each one has its own API, its own status codes, its own settlement timing and its own quirks. Without proper integration, the result is manual work, delays and errors that are painful to unpick later.
* Brokers setting up their first payment methods ahead of launch
* Brokerages adding local payment options to grow in new regions
* Firms whose deposits still need someone to manually credit trading accounts
* Businesses that have lost a provider before and want backup routes in place
* Prop firms handling challenge fees on the way in and trader payouts on the way out
Payment Architecture

We plan how your payment providers fit together. Which methods serve which countries, which currencies each supports, where card payments go versus bank transfers or e-wallets, and how everything reports back into a single view. Good structure here saves a lot of patching later.
Deposit Workflow

A client chooses an amount and method in your client portal, completes payment on the provider's secure page, and once the provider confirms success, the funds appear on their trading account. Failed or abandoned payments are recorded too, so your support team can see exactly what happened when a client gets in touch.
Withdrawal Workflow

Withdrawal requests move into a review queue rather than going out automatically. Your finance team can check verification status, open positions, available margin, previous deposit methods and any rules you apply, such as returning funds to the original source first. Once approved, the payout is sent through the relevant provider and the client's balance updates.
Webhooks and Status Handling

Providers send real-time notifications when a payment succeeds, fails, is reversed or is still pending. We set your systems up to listen for these messages, verify they're genuine and act on them correctly, including handling duplicates and delayed callbacks without double-crediting anyone.
Reconciliation
Daily matching between what providers report, what your CRM recorded and what landed on trading accounts. Mismatches are flagged instead of quietly piling up until month end.
CRM and Balance Synchronisation
Every deposit and withdrawal is logged against the client profile in your CRM and reflected on their MT4 or MT5 account. Your finance, support and compliance teams all look at the same numbers.
Multiple Providers and Backup Routes

Payment providers sometimes go down, change their risk appetite or exit a market altogether. With more than one provider connected for key methods, you can route traffic elsewhere if one stops working. Routing can also follow country, currency or amount rules.
Security Setup

Card details are handled on the provider's own secure pages rather than passing through your servers, which keeps sensitive data out of your systems and reduces your exposure. API credentials are stored securely, callback endpoints are protected, and staff access to payment functions is limited by role.

Do you provide a forex payment gateway yourselves?
No. We integrate the payment providers you hold agreements with. The providers process the money, and we build the technical connections around them.
Can you help us find payment providers that accept forex brokers?
We can explain the technical considerations worth checking, such as supported methods, APIs, webhooks and settlement reporting. Commercial approval and terms are between you and each provider.
How quickly do deposits reach trading accounts?

Once the provider confirms a successful payment, the balance can update automatically. Overall timing depends on the payment method and the provider, since some methods confirm almost instantly while bank transfers can take longer.
Can withdrawals be fully automatic?
They can, but most brokers prefer an approval step for checks like verification status, open positions and source-of-funds rules. We set it up however your policy requires.
What happens if a payment provider goes offline?
If you have a backup provider connected for that method, routing can switch so clients can still deposit. Without one, that method is unavailable until the provider recovers.

In a standard setup, no. Clients enter card details on the provider's secure page, which keeps that data out of your systems.

Where you've agreed terms with a crypto payment provider that offers an API, yes. Regulatory treatment of crypto payments differs by jurisdiction, so check your obligations first.

Provider reports, CRM records and trading account balances are matched daily. Anything that doesn't line up is flagged so your finance team can investigate. This is one of the main benefits of a proper forex payment gateway integration.

blocks.text: A brokerage cares about deposits, trading activity and client retention. A prop firm's concerns sit somewhere else entirely. You're selling evaluations, measuring traders against strict rules, deciding who progresses, and paying out a share of profits to the ones who succeed.

Standard broker CRMs weren't built for that cycle. They don't know what a daily loss limit is, can't move a trader from phase one to phase two, and won't tell you that three accounts are copying each other's trades. Prop firms need tooling designed around evaluation logic, and that's what this is.
* New prop firms planning their first challenge programme
* Growing firms whose manual checks are starting to miss breaches or delay funded accounts
* Brokers adding a prop trading division alongside their regular business
* Firms moving to a new trading platform and needing their rules rebuilt properly
* Operators wanting to offer several challenge types, sizes and pricing tiers
Challenge and Evaluation Setup
Single-phase, two-phase, instant funding or custom models. You define account sizes, profit targets, minimum trading days, time limits, leverage and pricing for each, and the system handles the rest.
Checkout and Account Creation
Traders choose a challenge on your website, pay through your integrated payment provider and receive their trading account automatically. No one on your team has to create logins manually.
Trader Accounts and Progression

Each trader's journey is tracked from purchase through each phase to funded status. Passing a phase can trigger the next account automatically or send it for review first, whichever your process requires.
Rule Configuration

Daily loss limits, maximum drawdown (static or trailing), profit targets, consistency rules, minimum days, news trading restrictions, weekend holding, lot size caps and more. Rules can differ between challenge types and phases.
Real-Time Rule Monitoring

The system checks trading activity against each account's rules as it happens. When a breach occurs, the account can be disabled automatically and the trader notified with the reason, so there's no argument about what happened or when.
Risk Monitoring

Dashboards flag patterns worth a closer look, such as identical trades across linked accounts, suspected copy trading, hedging between accounts, latency arbitrage behaviour or unusual concentration in a single instrument.
Performance Dashboards

Traders see their progress against targets and limits in a clear dashboard, which cuts down support questions. Your team sees firm-wide views of active challenges, pass rates, breach reasons and revenue.
Payout Review Workflow

Payout requests from funded traders arrive in a review queue with trading history, rule compliance and risk flags attached. Your team approves or queries each request, and approved payouts go out through your payment provider with a full record kept.
CRM and Admin Panel
Trader profiles, KYC status, purchase history, account history, support notes and communication logs in one place, with role-based access for support, risk and finance staff.
API Access

A documented API lets your website, affiliate system, payment providers, KYC service and trading platform exchange data with the CRM. Useful if you want a custom front end or need to plug in tools you already use.

Challenge types, rules, progression logic, risk flags, payout policy and integrations are mapped out in detail. You approve every rule before it's built, because a misconfigured rule is a support headache waiting to happen.

The CRM is connected to your trading platform, website checkout, payment and KYC providers. We test every challenge type with simulated trading, deliberately triggering each rule to confirm breaches, passes and progressions behave exactly as intended.

CRM and rule engine configuration, platform, payment and KYC integrations, API setup, testing, launch support and ongoing technical maintenance.

Your business model, challenge terms, rule definitions, pricing, payout decisions, trader agreements, marketing claims, and compliance with consumer protection, financial and tax rules in every market you serve. Trading platform licensing terms for prop firm use vary between providers and have changed in recent years, so confirm your arrangement directly with your platform provider. What is a prop firm CRM?

It's software built around the prop trading cycle. Challenge sales, account creation, rule enforcement, phase progression, risk monitoring and payout review, all in one system linked to your trading platform.
Can we create our own challenge rules?
Yes. Targets, drawdowns, daily limits, minimum days, time limits, consistency rules and trading restrictions are all configurable per challenge type and phase.
Is rule monitoring real time?
Trading data is checked continuously, so breaches can be detected and acted on as they happen rather than at the end of the day.
Can the system detect copy trading or account abuse?
It can flag patterns that suggest copy trading, cross-account hedging or other prohibited behaviour. Final decisions stay with your risk team.
Are payouts sent automatically?
They can be, but most firms prefer a review step. Requests come with trading history and risk flags attached so your team can decide quickly.
Which trading platforms does it connect to?
We review your chosen platform during design and confirm integration options. Platform availability for prop firms depends on each provider's current licensing terms.
Do you offer a prop firm API?
Yes. A documented API allows your website, affiliate tools and other systems to exchange data with the CRM, which helps if you want a custom front end or integrations of your own.
Can we start with one challenge type and add more later?
Absolutely. Many firms launch with a single programme, then add sizes, phases or instant funding options as they grow. Our prop firm CRM is built to expand with you.

Label: Our Delivery Process

Building the technology behind a brokerage involves a lot of moving parts, and many founders start without a clear idea of what happens when. That uncertainty is usually where budgets stretch and deadlines slip.

So here's our forex broker setup process laid out openly. Four stages, what happens inside each one, what we'll need from you along the way and what tends to slow projects down. Whether you need a full stack or a single piece of it, the same approach applies.

sections.title: The Four Stages at a Glance

blocks.text: 01 Consultation → 02 Solution Design → 03 Integration → 04 Launch & Support
Each stage ends with something concrete you can review before we move forward. Nothing gets built on assumptions, and you won't be asked to approve work you haven't seen.
This is where we get to know your business properly. It usually starts with a call, followed by a short questionnaire and, for larger projects, a few working sessions with your team.
What We Cover
* Your business model, whether that's a broker, a prop firm or a hybrid
* Target countries and the clients you expect to serve
* Execution approach and how you plan to handle order flow
* Platform preference, if you have one, or whether you'd like guidance
* Providers already signed or under discussion for liquidity, payments and verification
* Your timeline, including any regulatory milestones the launch depends on
* Budget range, so recommendations stay realistic
What You Get
A clear summary of your requirements, written back to you so we can both confirm we've understood the business correctly. If something you want isn't technically sensible, this is where we'll say so.
With the requirements agreed, we design the stack. This stage is mostly thinking and planning, and it's the one that saves the most money later.
Architecture Decisions

Which trading platform and licence model fits, MT5 or MT4, white label, grey label or full server. Where servers will be hosted. How liquidity connects, whether through a bridge, gateway or direct FIX. Which CRM, payment and verification providers plug in, and how data moves between them.
Workflow Mapping

How a client signs up, gets verified, funds, receives a trading account and withdraws. How introducing brokers are tracked and paid. Who on your team approves what. Mapping these journeys early shows up conflicts before they become bugs.
Project Plan
A timeline with milestones, responsibilities on both sides, dependencies on third-party providers and a breakdown of costs.
What You Get
A solution document covering architecture, workflows, integrations and schedule. You approve it, ask questions or request changes before any build work starts.
This is the build. Servers go up, platforms are configured and systems get connected to each other.
Infrastructure and Platform

Hosting environments are provisioned and secured. The trading platform is installed or set up under your chosen arrangement, with groups, symbols, account types and trading conditions configured to your specification.
Connectivity
Liquidity connections are established in a staging environment first, symbols are mapped and routing rules applied.
Operational Systems
Your CRM, verification provider, payment providers, website registration and any mobile app are connected to the platform and to each other.
Third-Party Coordination

Liquidity providers, payment companies and verification services each need credentials issued, test environments opened and sometimes certification completed. We handle the technical back-and-forth so you aren't stuck relaying messages between engineers.
Testing and Acceptance

Before anything goes live, we test the whole chain with realistic scenarios. Pricing accuracy, order execution, rejections, margin events, swaps, onboarding, deposits, withdrawals, partner commissions and reporting. Then your own team runs through their daily tasks in the test environment and signs off when satisfied. Anything that fails gets fixed and checked again.
What You Get
A fully working, tested environment and written confirmation of what was tested and passed.
Go-Live

We agree on a launch date and time, usually a quieter market period. Production credentials are switched on, monitoring is active, and our engineers are watching closely as the first real clients arrive.
Early Stabilisation

The opening weeks often reveal small things no test could predict, like a payment method behaving oddly in one country or a symbol setting that needs adjusting once real volume appears. We stay close during this period and fix issues quickly.
Ongoing Support

After stabilisation, you move onto a support arrangement covering monitoring, maintenance, configuration changes, updates and help when your team needs it. As your business grows, we add providers, markets, features and capacity.
What You Get
A live brokerage, documentation describing your setup, and a team that already understands your environment when you need changes later.
Projects run smoothly when a few things are in place on your side:
* A main contact who can make decisions or get them made quickly
* Signed agreements with liquidity, payment and verification providers, or progress toward them
* Branding assets such as logos, colours and fonts
* Your onboarding, withdrawal and risk policies, even in draft
* Time from your team for testing before launch
* Clarity on your regulatory position and any conditions attached to it
Being upfront about this helps you plan.
Provider Onboarding
Payment companies and liquidity providers often run their own due diligence on your business. That can take longer than the technical work itself.
Late Changes
Switching platform, provider or business model mid-build means revisiting design and sometimes redoing integration work.
Regulatory Timing
If launch depends on licence approval, the technology may be ready before you're legally able to go live. Planning for this is better than rushing at the end.
Testing Squeezed for Time
When go-live dates are fixed and earlier stages run late, testing is the first thing people want to cut. We'd strongly advise against it.
Our Role
Technical consultation, solution design, infrastructure, platform configuration, connectivity, integrations, testing, launch support and ongoing maintenance.
Your Role
Business decisions, company formation, licensing, compliance policies, commercial agreements with providers, banking, marketing and client service.
Third Parties

Platform developers, liquidity providers, payment companies and verification services operate under their own terms and timelines. We coordinate the technical side with them, but their approvals and service levels are their own. We're not affiliated with or endorsed by the MT4 or MT5 platform developer unless clearly stated. Regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction, so take qualified legal advice for your markets.
How long does the full forex broker setup process take?

It depends on scope, platform choice and how quickly providers complete their own onboarding. A white label with standard integrations moves faster than a full deployment with several providers. You'll get a realistic estimate at the end of solution design.
Can we skip stages if we already have some systems?
Yes. If you already run a platform or CRM, we focus on the pieces you need and connect them to what's already working.
Do I need my licence before starting?
Not necessarily. Many clients run the technology build in parallel with their licence application. Whether and which licence you need depends on your jurisdiction and business model.
What does the MT5 broker setup process involve specifically?

Choosing a licence arrangement, configuring server groups, symbols and trading conditions, connecting liquidity, linking your CRM and payment systems, and testing everything before launch. It forms one part of the wider integration stage.
Will we see progress during the build?
Yes. Each stage ends with a deliverable for your review, and you'll have regular updates throughout integration.
What happens after launch?
We monitor closely during early trading, resolve issues quickly and then move you onto ongoing support for maintenance, changes and growth.
Can you guarantee a launch date?

We'll commit to our own milestones, but final dates also depend on third-party providers and regulatory timing that sit outside our control. Our forex broker setup process is built to surface those dependencies early so there are fewer surprises.
Tell us what you're planning and where you are today. We'll walk you through how the process would apply to your brokerage, what decisions come first and roughly how long each stage should take.

Label: Questions & Answers

Brokerage technology comes with its own vocabulary, and it's easy to feel lost between gateways, grey labels and webhooks. This forex broker technology FAQ gathers the questions founders, operators and prop firm owners ask us most, answered in plain language.
Can't see your question here? Ask us directly and we'll give you a straight answer.

items.q: What does a forex technology provider actually do?
items.a: We build, connect and maintain the systems a brokerage depends on. That covers trading platforms, servers, liquidity connections, CRMs, payment and verification integrations, apps and APIs. The brokerage runs the business, and we make sure the technology underneath it works.

items.q: Are you a broker or a liquidity provider?
items.a: Neither. We're purely a technology company. We don't execute client trades, provide liquidity, hold client money or offer investment advice.

items.q: Do I have to buy everything from you?
items.a: No. Some clients use us for one service, such as hosting or a CRM. Others hand us the whole stack. We're happy to work alongside systems and vendors you already have.

items.q: Can you help if I don't know where to start?
items.a: Yes, and plenty of our clients begin exactly there. During the first consultation we'll help you work out what you need, in what order and roughly what it involves.

items.q: Can you help us get a licence?
items.a: Licensing is a legal and regulatory matter, so it's outside what we do. We can explain how technology decisions interact with common regulatory expectations, but you'll need qualified advisors in your target jurisdiction for the licence itself.

items.q: Which markets do you work with?
items.a: We support brokerages serving clients in many regions. Where your clients are located does affect choices like hosting location, payment methods and verification providers, which we factor into the design.

items.q: Should a new broker choose MT5 or MT4?
items.a: Most new brokers now choose MT5. It supports more asset classes, has a more modern architecture and is where the platform developer focuses ongoing work. MT4 still has a loyal user base, so some brokers offer both.

items.q: Can we run MT4 and MT5 at the same time?
items.a: Yes. Many brokers do, either permanently or during a gradual move from one to the other. The two can share liquidity connections and a CRM.

items.q: How hard is it to move from MT4 to MT5?
items.a: It takes careful planning rather than heavy lifting. Account types, groups, symbols and trading conditions need recreating, integrations need reconnecting and clients need a clear transition path. Phased migrations tend to go smoothest.

items.q: Are you affiliated with the MetaTrader platform developer?
items.a: No, not unless we state otherwise for a specific arrangement. We work with the platforms as a technology provider.

items.q: What is an MT5 white label?
items.a: It's an arrangement where your brokerage runs on MT5 under your own brand, inside an environment operated under an existing platform licence. You get branded access and your own account setup without buying a full server licence yourself.

items.q: Why would a broker choose white label over a full licence?
items.a: Mainly cost and speed. A full licence carries a large upfront investment and more technical responsibility. A white label lets you launch sooner and spend less, with the option to move to your own server later.

items.q: Can I control my own spreads and account types on a white label?
items.a: Usually, yes, within the limits of the arrangement and your liquidity setup. Exactly how much control you get varies by provider, so it's worth confirming before signing.

items.q: Does a white label give me permission to operate as a broker?
items.a: No. It's a technology arrangement only. Financial licensing is completely separate.

items.q: What is a grey label?
items.a: A grey label generally sits more directly under another provider's infrastructure and arrangement, with lower entry costs and less independent control than a white label. Terms vary widely between providers, so definitions aren't always consistent.

items.q: What's the main difference between white label and grey label?
items.a: In broad terms, a white label gives you more control over branding and configuration, while a grey label trades some of that control for a lighter, cheaper setup. We'll explain exactly what any specific offer includes before you commit.

items.q: Is a grey label right for my business?
items.a: It can suit smaller or early-stage operations testing the market with limited budget. If you expect fast growth or need detailed control over trading conditions, a white label or full deployment is often a better long-term fit.

items.q: Does a grey label mean I don't need a company or licence?
items.a: Not necessarily. Requirements depend on your jurisdiction, business model and the provider's terms. Take legal advice rather than relying on general claims.

items.q: What does a forex CRM do?
items.a: It manages the whole client journey. Lead capture, registration, identity verification, deposits, withdrawals, trading account creation, partner commissions and reporting, usually with a client portal on top.

items.q: Can the CRM connect with MT5?
items.a: Yes. It links to MT5 and MT4 through manager API access, so trading accounts are created, balances updated and trading data pulled in automatically.

items.q: Can it handle introducing broker commissions?
items.a: Yes. Rebate rules are set in the CRM, which then calculates earnings from real trading data, including multi-level partner structures.

items.q: Can we move our data from our current CRM?
items.a: In most cases, yes. We map fields between the two systems, run test imports and check records carefully before switching over.

items.q: What is a liquidity bridge?
items.a: It's software that sits between your trading platform and one or more liquidity providers, passing prices in and orders out. Bridges typically add tools like markups, routing rules and multi-provider pricing.

items.q: What's the difference between a bridge, a gateway and FIX?
items.a: A gateway is a more direct link between MT5 and an external system. A bridge is separate middleware with extra routing and aggregation features. FIX is the messaging protocol that both commonly use to communicate with providers.

items.q: Can I connect more than one liquidity provider?
items.a: Yes. Multiple providers can be aggregated for pricing or set up as backups for each other.

items.q: Can you guarantee spreads or execution quality?
items.a: No. Pricing and fills come from your providers and depend on market conditions. What we make sure of is that the technical link carrying them is accurate and well monitored.

items.q: Do you provide MT4 and MT5 hosting?
items.a: Yes. We host both, along with environments where they run side by side.

items.q: Where should our trading server be?
items.a: Typically near your main liquidity providers, with client access points closer to where your clients trade. Data rules in your markets can also influence the decision.

items.q: What happens if a server fails?
items.a: Your disaster recovery plan kicks in. Depending on your setup, a standby server takes over or the environment is restored from tested backups.

items.q: Can you guarantee uptime?
items.a: No honest provider can. We reduce risk through monitoring, redundancy, tested backups and a fast response when issues arise.

items.q: Do you process client payments?
items.a: No. Payment providers process the money. We integrate them with your CRM and trading platform so deposits and withdrawals flow properly.

items.q: Can you connect our existing payment and KYC providers?
items.a: Usually, yes, as long as they offer usable integration options. We confirm this during the design stage.

items.q: Does your verification integration make us compliant?
items.a: No technology can do that alone. It gives your compliance team the workflow and records they need, but compliance obligations stay with your business.

items.q: Do you build technology for prop firms?
items.a: Yes. That includes challenge setup, automated account creation, rule monitoring, risk flags, performance dashboards and payout review workflows.

items.q: Can we have a branded mobile trading app?
items.a: Yes. We build iOS and Android apps under your brand, connected to your platform, CRM, payments and verification. Publication is subject to app store review.

items.q: Can you integrate APIs?
items.a: Yes. We work with manager APIs, payment and verification APIs, webhooks and custom integrations between your systems and third-party tools.

items.q: Do you offer PAMM and MAM solutions?
items.a: Yes. We provide PAMM and MAM technology for brokers that support money managers, integrated with MT4 or MT5.

items.q: How long does setup take?
items.a: It depends on scope, platform choice and how quickly third-party providers complete their onboarding. You'll get a realistic timeline after the solution design stage.

items.q: What do you need from us to get started?
items.a: A clear point of contact, an outline of your business model, details of any providers you've chosen and your target timeline. We'll guide you through the rest.

items.q: What support do you offer after launch?
items.a: Monitoring, maintenance, configuration changes, updates and technical help, under a support arrangement agreed with you before go-live.

items.q: Do we keep ownership of our systems and data?
items.a: Yes. Your data and your accounts with third-party providers remain yours, and every change we make is documented.

items.q: Still have a question that isn't covered here?
items.a: Get in touch. This forex broker technology FAQ grows over time based on what clients ask, so your question may help the next person too.
